sc: Unvaccinated child, grey membrane that bleeds when removed, bull neck → Diphtheria: antitoxin + penicillin
2-month-old with coughing spells and apnoea, no whoop → Pertussis: admit
Unvaccinated child, fever, asymmetric flaccid leg weakness, normal sensation → Polio (AFP)
f: Membrane, bull neck · death from myocarditis · palatal palsy (nasal regurgitation) at 3 weeks · antitoxin early + penicillin 14 days
Catarrhal → paroxysmal cough with whoop, vomiting after cough · lymphocytosis · infants: apnoea · azithromycin 5 days
Lockjaw, spasms, fully conscious · tetanus immunoglobulin 500 IU · metronidazole · diazepam · vaccinate after recovery
Any child < 15 yr with sudden flaccid weakness: notify + 2 stool samples · polio: asymmetric, no sensory loss
Diphtheria vs EBV (splenomegaly, atypical lymphs) · polio vs Guillain–Barré (symmetric, ascending, high CSF protein)
Pentavalent at 6, 10, 14 wk · OPV/IPV · Td to mothers (neonatal tetanus)
trap: Main cause of death in diphtheria is myocarditis, not the airway · infants with pertussis may only have apnoea · recovery from tetanus does not give immunity
